[Weak, RPE 4/10] Feels like 34C. Garmin classified Tempo (High Aerobic), Aerobic TE 3.6. GCT highest recorded at the time - fatigue signature. Not quite in form per athlete; attributed to accumulated fatigue from big prior week (18km long run) plus heat, not fitness decline.

[Normal, RPE 4/10] Recovery run following 16 Jul fatigue-flagged session. Garmin classified Base (Low Aerobic), Aerobic TE 3.1. Confirmed fatigue theory - faster pace and lower HR than 2 days prior after rest.

[Strong, RPE 3/10] Fastest sustained treadmill pace recorded to date. Personal bests in GCT (243ms) and stride length (1.02m). Garmin classified Base (Low Aerobic), Aerobic TE 3.6, Exercise Load 128. Faster than typical Phase 1 base effort - closer to tempo-adjacent.

[Weak, RPE 5/10] Last day of 4-day consecutive training block (~35-36km for the week, no rest day). Accumulated fatigue confirmed. Garmin classified Base (Low Aerobic). Coach flagged need for at least 1 rest day per week going forward.

[Strong, RPE 3/10] Recovery confirmed following rest day after 22 Jul fatigue. Nearly identical pace/HR to 22 Jul but completely different subjective feel (Strong vs Weak, 3/10 vs 5/10 effort) - proof previous dip was fatigue not fitness decline. Garmin classified Base (Low Aerobic), Aerobic TE 3.7. Goblet squats + lunges done same day.

[Strong, RPE 3/10] Best clean Zone 2 data point in recent stretch - broke plateau after two flat readings (22 Jul, 24 Jul). Gap to target pace (6:10-6:15/km) narrowed to +22-27 sec, best yet. Garmin classified Base (Low Aerobic), Aerobic TE 3.6.

[Strong, RPE 3/10] Best distance-pace-HR combination long run to date. Recovery HR 31 bpm (strong fitness signal). Weather good. Garmin classified Tempo (High Aerobic), Aerobic TE 4.4, Exercise Load 196. Run/walk strategy used - walk break for water approximately every 3km, timer kept running (continuous, not paused) unlike 11 Jul run. HR stayed controlled at Zone 2/3 boundary rather than clear Zone 3 overshoot seen on 11 Jul.

[EVENING START 18:14 — corrected 11 Aug; the test was run in evening heat, which elevates HR at a given effort, so LTHR 176 may sit 1-2 bpm high] [very_weak, RPE 5/10] LTHR FIELD TEST — 30-min field test, average HR of final 20 min. Window 3.83km in 20:01 @ 5:14/km -> LTHR 176 (Garmin auto-detect). Pace faded 5:05 -> 5:22 across the window while HR climbed to 179 — effort sat at or just above threshold, which is what a valid test should look like. Logged Feel as 'Very Weak' at only RPE 5/10; flag if this recurs, since it may indicate the HR reading was elevated by fatigue or illness rather than by effort. EF excluded: Activity started cold with no warm-up (HR 80 bpm at t=0). Whole-run EF is distorted by the ramp and is not comparable to steady Z2 sessions.

[strong, RPE 3/10] Evening run in heat. Z3-dominant, not Z2 - initially misclassified from the 157 mean before time-in-zone was available. Cadence 175 and VO 8.0 were both step changes from the deliberate posture cue introduced this day. Ran 24h after the LTHR test.

[strong, RPE 2/10] Best power-to-HR of the block at 1.61 W/bpm. Power zones read easy (48% Z1, 46% Z2) while HR zones read moderate - the gap is accumulated fatigue from three consecutive days. Cadence drifted back to 169 as the force cue was deliberately rationed.
[normal, RPE 3/10] Fourth consecutive day. This run established the three-consecutive-day maximum as a firm rule.
[weak, RPE 4/10] Later start (07:42) than the surrounding morning runs. Athlete reported the heat was bad this day.
[strong, RPE 3/10] Cleanest easy-run execution to date. Avg 148, max 160, Base label, RPE 3.

[strong, RPE 3/10] Progressive long run with a fast finish, not a flat easy run - first ~50 min below average pace, closing segments at 5:50-6:00/km. Mantra adopted this run: 'Think light, quick steps, arms down.'
